## Hard Principles

1. Security-first: file validation, input sanitization, RBAC. **All generated or edited code must satisfy §OWASP Top 10 Compliance below** — that checklist is binding, not advisory. Security review before completion.
2. RBAC enforced at controller (`@Secured`) AND in UI.
3. Schema = Flyway migrations + Hibernate auto-update. **New entities must declare
   `@GeneratedValue(strategy = GenerationType.IDENTITY)`** — a bare `@GeneratedValue`
   resolves to a native `<table>_seq` that fights an `AUTO_INCREMENT` column and yields
   intermittent `Duplicate entry '<n>' for key 'PRIMARY'`. See `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`
   §Entity id generation.
4. Always write tests. Source of truth for credentials and URLs is `pass-cli`.
5. **A change is complete only when** `./gradlew build` is clean **AND** `./scripts/startbackenddev.sh` starts cleanly. Compile-clean ≠ runtime-clean (Micronaut bean wiring, Flyway, SessionFactory only check at startup). Stop the backend after verifying.
5a-relay. **Relay changes (`src/relay/`) are complete only when** `cd src/relay && go build ./... && go vet ./... && gofmt -l . && go test ./...` are all clean. It is a separate Go module: `./gradlew build` does not compile it and will not catch a break. It has **no third-party dependencies by contract** — adding one needs a stated reason in the PR body, the same bar as `src/clinotify`.
5a. **Frontend changes are complete only when** `cd src/frontend && npm ci && npm run build` exits 0. TypeScript errors, missing imports, and broken Astro/React components are caught here — do not skip this step for any frontend file edit.
5b. **Backend contract changes are complete only when the `extensions/` clients are updated in the same change.** Renaming a path, renaming or retyping a request/response field, tightening `@Secured`, or altering the auth scheme breaks those clients **silently** — nothing in this build compiles or tests against them, so the failure surfaces in production, not in CI. See **Extension Clients** for the surface and the verification rules. `/finalizer` automates the check.
6. Normal-stack tests route HTTP through `SECMAN_HOST` (from `pass-cli`). Database-mutating E2E tests use only the URLs and restricted database supplied by `./scripts/test/run-isolated-e2e.sh`; never hardcode a test URL in a driver.
7. **Mandatory post-change E2E gates** (in addition to build + startup):
   - **`/e2ejs`** must report **0 JS errors** for both admin and normal-user runs against `SECMAN_HOST`. RBAC 403s on role-gated endpoints and documented 404s (e.g., `/api/wg-vulns`, `/api/domain-vulns` for users without mappings) are NOT JS errors. A page that throws or logs `console.error` IS — fix before merge.
   - **`/e2evulnexception`** must run the full vuln + exception lifecycle (MCP + UI, setup + teardown) with **0 failures**.

   Doc-only edits outside `src/`, `tests/`, `scripts/` may skip the gates — state so explicitly. Otherwise both gates are non-negotiable.

## OWASP Top 10 Compliance (mandatory)

Hard Principle 1 in concrete terms. **Do not generate code that violates any rule below.** Categories are pinned to **OWASP Top 10:2021 (A01–A10)**; if the list is revised upstream, revisit this section rather than silently re-mapping names.

Each rule names the control that already exists in this repo. **Reuse it — never write a second one**, and never work around one to make something build, start or pass.

**A01 Broken Access Control**
- Every endpoint carries `@Secured`. A public endpoint is an explicit, justified exception (`GET /api/crowdstrike/last-checkin`, `GET /api/maintenance-banners/active`), never a default and never "for now".
- An id in a request is untrusted input. Resolve assets through `AssetFilterService.getAccessibleAssets()` / `getAccessibleAssetIds()` / `canAccessAsset(assetId, authentication)` — never `findById(userSuppliedId)` and return it. Same for any other owner-scoped entity.
- SQL pre-filters in materialized views and native queries are perf hints, **never the auth boundary** (restated from §Unified Asset Access — it is the single most repeated bug class here).
- A new MCP tool needs entries in **both** `McpToolPermissions.LISTING` and `.CALLING` plus a `McpToolGuards` check. A missing `CALLING` entry fails closed and looks like a bug; a missing guard fails **open** and looks like nothing.
- RBAC at the controller **and** in the UI (Principle 2). The UI check is UX; the controller check is the boundary. Never only the former.

**A02 Cryptographic Failures**
- Passwords and API-key secrets: `BCryptPasswordEncoder` only. Never SHA-256/MD5/hand-rolled hashing for a secret — the SHA-256 API-key path in `McpAuthenticationService` exists solely to migrate legacy keys, do not extend or imitate it.
- The JWT lives in the HttpOnly `secman_auth` cookie. Never write a token to `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, a non-HttpOnly cookie, or any value that lands in a log. The SSE `?token=` query param is the one documented exception (EventSource has no headers).
- Secrets come from `pass-cli`/env. No literal credential, key, token or internal host in source, tests, scripts or fixtures.
- `JwtSigningValidator`, `DatabaseCredentialValidator` and `DatasourceUrlValidator` fail the boot on weak config **by design** — never relax or bypass one to make the backend start.

**A03 Injection**
- Persistence: derived queries or bound parameters (`:name`) only. **Never** concatenate a value into a query string — this includes the ~30 `nativeQuery = true` methods in `VulnerabilityRepository`, `WorkgroupRepository`, `AwsAccountSharingRepository`. Things that cannot be bound (column name, sort direction, table) map through a closed allowlist/enum; a request value never reaches SQL unbound.
- HTML: no `innerHTML` / `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` without `DOMPurify.sanitize(...)` **at the assignment site** — see `RichContent.tsx` and `HtmlEditor.tsx`. Sanitizing on write is not sufficient: stored rows predate the control.
- Excel/CSV export: every user-controlled cell goes through `ExcelSanitizer.sanitize()` (formula/DDE injection). No E2E gate ever opens an exported file, so a regression here is invisible at runtime and only `ExcelSanitizerTest` will catch it.
- OS: no user-controlled string interpolated into a shell command, from Kotlin or from `./scripts/`. Pass argv arrays; quote every variable in bash.
- Strip or encode CR/LF from user input before it reaches a log line (log forging).

**A04 Insecure Design**
- Deny by default: a new endpoint or MCP tool starts from the narrowest role that works and is widened deliberately — not `IS_AUTHENTICATED` with a TODO.
- Unbounded is a design bug: page at the query (`findByAssetIdIn(ids, pageable)`), never `findAll()` then filter/slice in Kotlin. That exact pattern OOM'd `get_vulnerabilities` on 1.1M rows.
- Business invariants (release status transitions, exception `kind`/subject/scope validity, ownership, workgroup membership) are enforced server-side. A rule that exists only in the UI is not a rule.

**A05 Security Misconfiguration**
- Do not weaken `SecurityHeadersFilter` — CSP, HSTS, `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, COOP/COEP/CORP, permissions policy. If a feature "requires" `unsafe-eval` or a wildcard `connect-src`, change the feature.
- CORS: explicit origin allowlist. Never `*` combined with credentials.
- Error responses carry a generic message; the detail goes to the server log. Never return a stack trace, SQL string, internal path or driver message to a client (`ValidationExceptionHandler` is the pattern).
- No debug endpoint, verbose-logging toggle or seeded default credential enabled outside the `test` profile.

**A06 Vulnerable and Outdated Components**
- Prefer the stdlib and dependencies already on the classpath. A new third-party dependency needs a stated reason and must be called out in the PR body.
- Pin exact versions in the Gradle/npm manifests — no floating ranges, no `latest`. `package-lock.json` must stay in step with `package.json` (`npm ci` is the gate).
- `src/clinotify` is **stdlib-only by contract**; adding a dependency there breaks its deployment.

**A07 Identification and Authentication Failures**
- Authenticate through `AuthenticationProviderUserPassword`, `OAuthService` or `McpAuthenticationService`. Never a bespoke auth path, and never a header that grants access on its own: `X-MCP-User-Email` *identifies* a delegated user, it is not a credential and must always sit behind a verified API key.
- Login, password-reset and lookup errors must not disclose whether an account exists.
- Password change stays LOCAL-account-only; MFA state stays server-enforced.
- Never lengthen a token/session lifetime, or loosen a cookie's `HttpOnly`/`Secure`/`SameSite`, to fix a UX or test problem.

**A08 Software and Data Integrity Failures**
- Every upload validates **size, extension and content type before parsing**, and rejects empty files — `ImportController.validateFile` is the reference; keep `MAX_FILE_SIZE` aligned with `application.yml`.
- XML parsing keeps DTDs and external entities **disabled** (XXE). `NmapParserService`/`MasscanParserService` set `disallow-doctype-decl`, `external-general-entities`, `external-parameter-entities` and `load-external-dtd` — copy that block into any new XML parser; never construct a bare `DocumentBuilderFactory`.
- Never deserialize untrusted input into a polymorphic or arbitrary type — parse into an explicit DTO.
- Never fetch code, config or a template from a remote source at runtime and execute or eval it.
- Archive handling: reject entry paths containing `..` and bound the decompressed size (zip bomb).

**A09 Security Logging and Monitoring Failures**
- Log authentication failures, RBAC denials, admin actions, imports and exports with **actor + target + outcome**.
- Never log a password, token, cookie value, API key, or the body of an auth request. `logger.debug` counts — it runs in dev, where real `pass-cli` secrets are loaded.
- No silent `catch (e: Exception) { }`. A swallowed security-relevant failure is itself a monitoring failure.

**A10 Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)**
- Any outbound URL derived from user input or DB-stored config — identity provider endpoints and JWKS, GitHub App, CrowdStrike, S3 endpoints, notification webhooks — is validated before use: `https` scheme allowlist, plus host allowlist or explicit rejection of loopback, link-local and RFC-1918 ranges and cloud metadata (`169.254.169.254`).
- Re-apply the same check to redirect targets; never follow a redirect into a range the original request would have been denied.
- `McpOriginValidationFilter` is the inbound analogue — do not disable it.

### Review gate

Before reporting any code change complete, run `./scripts/owasp-check.sh` (diff-scoped, includes untracked files) and re-read the diff against A01–A10, then state the result in one line, e.g. `OWASP: A01/A03/A09 touched — clean`. A `BLOCK` finding means the change is not complete; a `REVIEW` finding needs a stated decision, not silence. Changes to authentication, authorization, crypto, file upload, export or any outbound HTTP call additionally run `/security-review` on the branch diff (`/finalizer` includes a HIGH/CRITICAL pass). **A finding at HIGH or above blocks the change** — fix it, do not merely note it.

The scanner covers only the mechanical half. Use **`/secure-code`** *before* writing an endpoint, query, MCP tool, upload, export, HTML sink or outbound call: it routes the change to the categories it can actually violate, names the existing control to reuse, and carries the semantic checklist the scanner cannot express.

## Patterns (worth knowing)

Code samples in `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §Patterns — CSV/Excel import (validate → parse → header check → row parse → dedupe → batch save → `ImportResult`), asset merge (`findByName` → append groups, update IP, preserve owner; else create), event-driven (`@EventListener @Async`), OAuth state retry (`OAuthService.findStateByValueWithRetry`, `OAUTH_STATE_RETRY_*`). Memory optimization: `MemoryOptimizationConfig` reads `secman.memory.*`, monitor `GET /memory`, any toggle `false` rolls back. Env names: `docs/ENVIRONMENT.md`.

### Auth
- Backend: `@Secured(SecurityRule.IS_AUTHENTICATED)` + `authentication.roles.contains("…")`.
- Frontend: the JWT lives in the **HttpOnly `secman_auth` cookie** (`AuthCookieService.AUTH_COOKIE_NAME`), not in JS-readable storage. Axios sends it via `withCredentials: true` (set globally in `utils/csrf.ts`); fetch calls use the `authenticated*` helpers in `utils/auth.ts` / `services/`. `sessionStorage["user"]` holds only the display/role payload — never a token.
- External/CLI clients: `POST /api/auth/login` returns the JWT **only** in `Set-Cookie: secman_auth=…`; clients either retain that cookie or extract the token and re-send it as `Authorization: Bearer …` (both readers stay active).
- SSE: JWT in `?token=…` query param (EventSource has no header support).

### Chat notifications (Slack / Telegram)
Publishers stay transport-agnostic: publish a `ChatNotificationEvent` where the work completes;
`ChatNotificationEventListener` (`@EventListener @Async`) → `ChatNotificationService` does
subscriber lookup, destination resolution and rendering. **A new reportable event = one
`NotificationEventType` constant + one publish call** (both settings APIs, both settings UIs and
the dispatcher derive from the enum). Subscriptions are `(user_id, channel, event_type)` rows, so
a new event or channel needs no migration and per-channel saves never disturb each other.
Dispatch must stay non-`@Transactional` — it does per-recipient HTTP with a multi-second timeout.
**Security**: the per-user Slack webhook URL is the only user-supplied URL the backend fetches —
host-allowlisted in `SlackClient.validateWebhookUrl`, redirects never followed. The Telegram bot
token goes in the request URL *path*, so `TelegramClient.validateBotToken` is a security control,
not input hygiene. All credentials use `EncryptedStringConverter`, are never returned (only
`…Configured` booleans), and accept `***HIDDEN***` back to mean "keep". Telegram sends with no
`parse_mode` on purpose. CrowdStrike completion is detected by a quiet-period debounce in
`ImportCompletionNotifier` (no last batch exists), AWS account imports publish inline post-commit.

### Transactional replace (CrowdStrike vuln import)
Per server: `findOrCreateAsset` → `vulnerabilityRepository.deleteByAssetId()` → `saveAll`, all in one `@Transactional`. Idempotent; missing CVEs in the next import = remediation.

**CRITICAL**: `Asset.vulnerabilities` MUST NOT use `cascade=ALL` or `orphanRemoval=true`. JPA cascade fights the manual delete-insert and silently drops 99% of rows (real incident: 166,812 → 1,819). Use explicit `vulnerabilityRepository.deleteByAssetId()` in the service. See `docs/CROWDSTRIKE_IMPORT.md`.

## Test Infrastructure

JUnit 6, Mockk, AssertJ, `@MicronautTest`. Integration tests run against an **external MariaDB** (no Docker/Testcontainers). **`junit-jupiter-params` is not on the classpath** — `@ParameterizedTest` will not compile; loop inside a plain `@Test`. Helpers in `src/backendng/src/test/kotlin/com/secman/testutil/`:
- `BaseIntegrationTest` — base for DB-backed tests; datasource comes from `application-test.yml`.
- `TestDataFactory` — admin/vuln/regular user, asset, vulnerability builders.
- `TestAuthHelper` — JWT login → bearer token.

Run backend tests through `./scripts/runbackendtests.sh` or wrap Gradle with `./scripts/test/run-isolated-e2e.sh --database-only --`. The runner creates and owns a fresh MariaDB schema, sets `TEST_DB_*`, and removes it after the run. Direct Gradle tests without its ownership marker fail before execution.

```kotlin
class MyIntegrationTest : BaseIntegrationTest() { @Inject lateinit var repo: Repository }
```

**Frontend unit tier**: `cd src/frontend && npm test` — Node's own runner with native
TypeScript stripping, no test-framework dependency. Tests live beside their module as
`<module>.test.ts`. Imports resolve `.ts` only: Node cannot parse JSX, so pure logic
must be extracted out of `.tsx` into a sibling `.ts` module to be unit-testable (the
resolver hook in `src/frontend/test/` handles extensionless specifiers and raises a
pointed error on `.tsx`). Details in `docs/TESTING.md` §Frontend.

No persistent `secman_test` setup is needed. Existing application rows are never test input or cleanup targets.

## File Layout

`src/backendng/…/com/secman/{domain,controller,service,repository,config,dto,filter,mcp,relay}/` · `src/frontend/src/{pages,components,services,layouts}/` · `src/cli/…/com/secman/cli/{commands,service}/` · `src/shared/…/com/secman/crowdstrike/{client,dto,auth,model}/` (Gradle subproject shared by backendng + cli) · `src/relay/{cmd,internal,deploy}/` (Go). `application.yml` + `email-templates/` under `src/backendng/src/main/resources/`. Env: `docs/ENVIRONMENT.md`. Full tree: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §File layout.

## Extension Clients (`extensions/`)

`secman_ai_github`, `secman_web_check`, and `secman_intra_mon` are independent Python repositories with their own remotes, **gitignored here** — root `git status` never shows them. Normal builds do not cover them. The first two share the version-1 result contract covered by `/integration-contract-test` and `scripts/check-integration-contract.sh --run`; `secman_intra_mon` uses the legacy REST surface and needs the same manual five-dimension contract check described below.

`secman_app_ios` (iOS/iPadOS status app, Swift) is a **relay client, not a backend client**: it never calls `/api/…` and holds no secman credential. A change to a secman endpoint cannot break it. What *can* is the relay contract — `com.secman.relay.RelayDtos`, the section names and `SECTION_POLICIES` in `RelaySnapshotBuilder`, or `src/relay/internal/api`. Both envelopes carry a `schemaVersion` for that reason; bump it on a breaking change and update `relaySupportedSnapshotSchemaVersion` in the app. Sweep its surface with `grep -rnE '/api/v1/|/ingest/v1/' extensions/secman_app_ios --include='*.swift'`.

Always rediscover the surface; a written list means a newly added call gets checked by nobody:
```bash
grep -rnE '/api/|"/mcp"|X-MCP-User-Email' extensions --include='*.py' --exclude-dir=.venv
```
As of 2026-09-25: legacy calls remain `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/vulnerabilities/cli-add`, `PUT /api/assets/import`, and `POST /api/scan/upload-nmap`. Version 1 uses `GET /api/integrations/v1/scanners/{id}/subjects` and `POST /api/integrations/v1/runs`; see `docs/INTEGRATION_RESULTS.md`.

When you change any of those endpoints, verify all five dimensions against the client: **path, HTTP method, request field names, response fields the client reads, and `@Secured` roles / required headers**. Field names matter most — Jackson drops unknown keys without error, so a rename makes the client "succeed" while sending nothing. Update the client's `tests/` too; a test asserting the old shape is drift.

Fix and commit **inside the extension repo, path-scoped** (`git -C extensions/<repo> commit -m "…" -- <files>`) so pre-existing dirty files are not swallowed. Never `git add -A` / `commit -a`, and **never push** — those repos have their own review. An `@Secured` tightening is a *report*, not a fix: you cannot see which roles the client's service account holds.

## E2E Runner

**Database safety:** Database-mutating test drivers must be invoked through
`./scripts/test/run-isolated-e2e.sh -- <driver and arguments>`. It creates a
marked disposable schema and restricted database user, copies schema structure
and Flyway history but no application rows, and starts a separate stack on
18080/14321. It cleans verified abandoned test schemas before a new run and
removes its own schema on exit. Direct driver calls fail closed. Do not delete
an unverified legacy fixture merely because its name matches a test prefix.
The normal 8080/4321 cold-start and stop rules below apply to read-only skills;
the isolated runner owns the lifecycle for mutating skills.

Triggered by `/e2eexception`, `/admin-asset-e2e`, `/e2ejs`, `/e2evulnexception`, `/e2eeol`, `/account-onboarding`, `/aws-account-workgroup-import`, `/importtest`, `/crowdstrike-vuln-match` skills.

- **Cold start for read-only skills**: stop the regular backend/frontend via the canonical stop scripts before restarting them. Database-mutating skills never stop or reuse that stack; the isolated runner starts and stops its own services.
- Backend changes (Kotlin/Java) → restart required.
- Frontend changes → Vite hot-reload (no restart).
- Config (`astro.config.mjs`, `application.yml`) → restart.
- Logs: `.e2e-logs/` (gitignored). Max 5 fix iterations.
- **Liveness check is port-bind**, not HTTP: `lsof -iTCP:8080 -sTCP:LISTEN -n -P` (120s budget) and `:4321` (60s budget).
- **Functional checks** use `SECMAN_HOST` for the regular stack or the runner-provided test-only URLs for isolated E2E. Never target regular 8080/4321 for a mutating test.

## Stack

- Backend: Kotlin 2.4.20 / Java 25, Micronaut 5.1, Hibernate JPA → `src/backendng/`
- Frontend: Astro 7.3 + React 19 islands, Axios, JWT in the HttpOnly `secman_auth` cookie → `src/frontend/`

- Mobile relay: Go 1.24, **zero third-party dependencies** (stdlib only, incl. its own RFC 8555 ACME client) → `src/relay/`
- DB: MariaDB 11.4, Flyway + Hibernate auto-migration
- Build: Gradle 9.7.1 (Kotlin DSL)
- MCP: Streamable HTTP / JSON-RPC 2.0. `X-MCP-User-Email` header is **mandatory** on `tools/list` and `tools/call` (only `initialize` and `ping` exempt).

CLAUDE.md:322:- **External web exposure and software-component inventory (2026-09-19)** — `secman_web_check` passively inventories JavaScript/CSS libraries, web servers, and scanner-vantage reachability from its own targets or SecMan-bound subjects, then prints, stores, or uploads atomic snapshots. SecMan provides asset-scoped REST/MCP reads and **Analytics → External exposure**; inventory stays separate from vulnerabilities and installed products. See `docs/INTEGRATION_RESULTS.md` and `docs/CHANGELOG.md`.
CLAUDE.md:324:- **Catch-all workgroup safety and direct workgroup links (2026-09-17)** — a configurable direct-user threshold now disables oversized catch-all workgroups without auto-re-enabling them; automatic disables invalidate access caches and are audited. User workgroup badges deep-link to the existing detail panel, and the workgroup table has Safari-safe sticky headers. See `docs/CHANGELOG.md`.
CLAUDE.md:326:- **CrowdStrike imports include domain controllers (2026-09-17)** — shared CrowdStrike scopes now include `DOMAIN_CONTROLLER` and composite `SERVER_FAMILY`; production vulnerability and product scripts use the composite scope and store discovered domain controllers as SecMan `SERVER` assets. See `docs/CROWDSTRIKE_IMPORT.md` and `docs/CHANGELOG.md`.
docs/CHANGELOG.md:29:- **Source-review quick wins: hot-path queries, transaction scope, dashboard parallelism (2026-08-27)** — first execution pass over `docs/SOURCE_REVIEW_COMPLEXITY_SPEED.md` §6. `AssetFilterService` admin paths use a new `findAllIds()` projection and the scan path became two batch queries (no more full-table `findAll()` + in-memory filter); eight `findAll().filter{hasRole}` sites became role queries; `NormMappingService` no longer holds a transaction across its OpenRouter loop (per-requirement apply transactions via self-`Provider`); the private CrowdStrike deadlock-retry copy merged into shared `DeadlockRetry`; new `GET /api/workgroups/tree` replaces the frontend's recursive per-node walk; home dashboard fetches run concurrently, the `McpDashboard` interval leak is fixed, dead `utils/api-config.ts` and the legacy unpaged `getCurrentVulnerabilities` are deleted. Backend build/startup + E2E gates still owed before merge (authoring env had no Gradle mirror/DB/pass-cli) — detail in `docs/CHANGELOG.md`.
docs/CHANGELOG.md:31:- **AWS account display names link accounts to workgroups (2026-08-25)** — an account whose `display_name` is `DevOps-x` now belongs to workgroup **`aws-DevOps-x`**: matched exactly (case-insensitively) on the `aws-` prefix, **created** when missing. One implementation, `WorkgroupAccountLinkService`, reached from the import (CLI/REST/MCP `displayName`, after the mappings commit) and from a correction path that re-links from stored names with no file — CLI `manage-user-mappings link-workgroups`, `POST /api/user-mappings/link-workgroup-accounts`, MCP `link_workgroup_aws_accounts`. The name is persisted as `user_mapping.aws_account_name` (V260) and deliberately kept **out** of the unique key. A display name that cannot be a workgroup name is an error row, never a forced creation; already-linked accounts are idempotent no-ops. Also fixed: six workgroup MCP tools were in `LISTING` but not `.CALLING` (listed yet uncallable). `docs/AWS_ACCOUNT_WORKGROUP_LINKING.md`.
docs/CHANGELOG.md:33:- **Full `excepted` recompute chunked to stop multi-minute lock holds (2026-08-24)** — `recomputeExceptedAll()` was one `UPDATE` with **no WHERE**, locking every `vulnerability` row (~1.8M) plus `vulnerability_exception` for 53-180s, so every concurrent writer (bulk exception delete/import, CrowdStrike import, per-asset recompute) queued behind it. `AsyncExceptionRecompute.recomputeAllChunked` now drives bounded **keyset** chunks (`CHUNK_SIZE` 10,000) through `recomputeExceptedForIdRange`, each its own REQUIRES_NEW transaction with per-chunk `DeadlockRetry`. Atomicity is deliberately given up (the path is already `@Async` and eventual); a failure now leaves a converged prefix. `recomputeExceptedAll()` is retained for integration tests only. `docs/CHANGELOG.md`.
docs/CHANGELOG.md:39:- **External web exposure and software-component inventory (2026-09-19)** — `extensions/secman_web_check` now derives a best-effort inventory from evidence the bounded HTTP collector already retrieved: conservative script and stylesheet URL signatures identify selected JavaScript/CSS libraries, and normalized `Server` signatures identify web servers. Detection never crawls or fetches a cross-origin resource merely to fingerprint it, and persisted/uploaded inventory stores no response body, cookie, credential, raw header value, URL query, or fragment. Each result carries an external-exposure observation explicitly tied to the `secman-web-check` vantage point; a failed or policy-denied collection stays `UNKNOWN` rather than claiming the site is down. Components and exposure now render in terminal, JSON schema 1.1, and the self-contained HTML report; MariaDB schema v2 adds exposure fields plus parameterized `scan_component` rows and component counts. `--targets-from-secman` reads the selected scanner's authorized integration subjects, skips subjects without a URI, retains exact subject/asset IDs, and uses that binding on upload instead of rematching a hostname; positional, text-file, and AWS CSV target modes remain available and mutually exclusive. The additive integration-run v1 `inventory` object is accepted only for `WEB_SECURITY`, validated at 500 components, hashed into retry identity, and stored immutably on the run. Current `web_exposure` and `web_component` rows update in the same transaction as findings; missing components resolve only after a newer successful inventory snapshot marked complete, independent of finding coverage. Asset-scoped REST adds `/api/integrations/v1/web-exposure/summary`, `/web-exposures`, and `/web-components`; MCP adds `get_web_exposure_summary`, `list_web_exposures`, and `list_web_components` in both permission maps with delegation, `INTEGRATIONS_READ`, and an ADMIN/VULN/SECCHAMPION guard. The same roles see **Analytics → External exposure**, with summary KPIs and paged asset/component tables. REST and MCP deliberately reuse one service; no SOAP adapter was added because SecMan has no SOAP consumer or reusable SOAP authentication/authorization boundary. Component inventory is not a vulnerability and is not written to `installed_product`; existing `WEB_SECURITY` findings still project under the generic `Webserver` product. Tests cover detection/redaction, reporting, local persistence, SecMan payload/direct binding, validation, atomic component lifecycle, MCP permissions/roles, and UI presentation.
docs/CHANGELOG.md:41:- **Catch-all workgroup safety and direct workgroup links (2026-09-17)** — application settings now expose a direct-user threshold for catch-all workgroups, defaulting to 100. Existing qualifying workgroups are disabled by migration, saving a new threshold immediately disables newly qualifying groups, and user-assignment/config-import paths re-check affected memberships server-side. The rule is fail-closed but never auto-enables a group after membership drops; an administrator must deliberately re-enable it. Disabled workgroups already grant no effective asset/account/domain access, and every automatic disable invalidates the workgroup-access cache and records actor, target, user count, threshold, and outcome. User Management workgroup badges now link to `/workgroups?workgroupId=…`, which opens the existing tree detail panel for that exact group. The workgroup table also uses WebKit-safe sticky header cells so Safari scrolling no longer paints rows through the header.
docs/CHANGELOG.md:43:- **CrowdStrike imports include domain controllers (2026-09-17)** — Falcon reports domain controllers under the separate exact `product_type_desc = 'Domain Controller'` category, so the production vulnerability and installed-product imports previously omitted them while querying only `Server`. The shared client now exposes `DOMAIN_CONTROLLER` and the composite `SERVER_FAMILY` scope; composite scopes issue bounded queries for each exact Falcon category and deduplicate agent IDs before the existing vulnerability pipeline runs. `ALL` now means Server + Domain Controller + Workstation. `scripts/import.sh`, `scripts/importaws.sh`, and `scripts/importproducts.sh` use `SERVER_FAMILY`, and the main import uses the documented 30-day last-seen window. Domain controllers deliberately persist as SecMan `SERVER` assets, retaining existing access, risk, KPI, notification, identity-conflict, and reconciliation behavior with no schema migration. Focused tests pin enum expansion, exact FQL filters, recency propagation, AID deduplication, and Discover product coverage.
docs/CHANGELOG.md:45:- **Web findings identify as findings and group under Webserver (2026-09-17)** — the current-vulnerabilities table now labels its identifier column **CVE/Finding**, reflecting that integration projections use stable finding identities rather than CVE identifiers. New `WEB_SECURITY` findings project `Webserver` into the Product field instead of exposing their internal external IDs there; V266 backfills both active vulnerability projections and the durable `integration_finding.projection_product` used when resolved findings reopen. The change is deliberately source-scoped: `VISUAL`, `GITHUB_AI`, CrowdStrike and manual vulnerabilities retain their existing product values, while the stable `INT:...` projection key remains unchanged for per-finding identity and exceptions. Product filters, statistics, exports, notifications and product-scoped exceptions consequently group these findings under `Webserver`.
docs/CHANGELOG.md:47:- **Source-review quick wins: hot-path queries, transaction scope, dashboard parallelism (2026-08-27)** — first execution pass over `docs/SOURCE_REVIEW_COMPLEXITY_SPEED.md` §6 (Phases 1–2). **Access-path queries**: the ADMIN/SECCHAMPION short-circuits in `AssetFilterService` now use a new `AssetRepository.findAllIds()` projection instead of materializing the whole asset table twice per request just to extract ids; the non-admin scan path replaced `scanRepository.findAll()` + in-memory uploader filtering (and a per-workgroup user-query loop) with two batch queries, `UserRepository.findByWorkgroupsIdInOrderByUsernameAsc` and `ScanRepository.findByUploadedByInOrderByScanDateDesc` — same predicate, same result set, no full-table scan. The documented-dead `getAccessibleVulnerabilities` (both branches were the full-table shape behind the 2026-07-30 heap incident) is deleted per its own comment; a tombstone comment remains. **Role lookups**: eight `userRepository.findAll().filter { hasRole }` sites across `UserService`, `UserDeletionValidator` (last-admin protection), `AdminNotificationService`, `CrowdStrikeCleanupNotificationService`, `ExceptionRequestNotificationService` and `ConfigBundleService` became `findByRolesContaining` / new `findByRolesContainingAny` / new `countByRolesContaining` — full user-table scans on notification and validation paths are gone; semantics identical (verified per site, `getUsersByRole` is now strictly narrower on unknown role strings). **Transaction scope**: `NormMappingService.suggestAndApplyMappings` no longer holds one transaction across its whole loop of multi-second OpenRouter calls — the AI phase runs untransacted and each requirement's mappings are applied in their own short transaction via a new `applyHighConfidenceSuggestions` reached through a self-`Provider` (the repo's standard AOP idiom); per-requirement failure isolation unchanged, entity re-loaded inside the transaction so nothing detached is saved. **Deadlock retry**: `CrowdStrikeVulnerabilityImportService`'s private `isDeadlockException`/`withDeadlockRetry` copy is deleted in favor of the shared `DeadlockRetry` (which had been lifted from it); the READ-COMMITTED rationale comment is preserved at the class, and the duplicated unit test dropped in favor of `DeadlockRetryTest`. **Workgroup tree**: new `GET /api/workgroups/tree` (`IS_AUTHENTICATED`, exactly the `/root`+`/children` visibility model via `accessibleWorkgroupIdsOrNull`) returns the caller's whole visible set flat with parent links; `MoveWorkgroupModal` now makes that one request instead of a serial recursive children-walk (one request per workgroup node). **Frontend**: `HomeStatisticsDashboard` runs its up-to-9 card fetches concurrently (latency = slowest, not sum) while keeping the deliberate per-card try/catch degradation; `McpDashboard`'s 30s poll no longer survives unmount (cleanup closed over a state variable that was still null at effect creation); `AssetManagement` memoizes its filtered list (previously recomputed 5× per render) and dropdown option sets; dead `utils/api-config.ts` (261 lines, zero importers) deleted; `VulnerabilityExceptionService`'s five copies of CVE-list parsing collapsed into `parseCveList`. **Removed**: `VulnerabilityService.getCurrentVulnerabilities` (legacy, `Pageable.UNPAGED` fetch-all-then-filter, zero production callers — everything uses `getCurrentVulnerabilitiesOptimized`/`getCurrentVulnerabilitiesByStatusSql`). Verification: frontend `npm ci && npm run build` clean + 257/0 unit tests; `owasp-check` 0 BLOCK (3 REVIEW decided in the PR); humanizer 0 BLOCK; `/security-review` no findings. **Backend Gradle build, backend startup and the two E2E gates could not run in the authoring environment (no Gradle distribution or dependency mirror reachable, no MariaDB, no pass-cli) — run `./gradlew build`, `./scripts/startbackenddev.sh`, `/e2ejs` and `/e2evulnexception` before merge.** Deferred by design, per the review's sequencing: email-out-of-transaction migration, hydration audit (needs `/e2ejs` per page), and all Phase-3 structural de-duplication.
docs/CHANGELOG.md:49:- **AWS account display names link accounts to workgroups (2026-08-25)** — an AWS account mapping file already names the team that owns each account (`display_name` in the Cloud Custodian export, a `display_name` column in the CSV exports), and that name was being thrown away at the CLI boundary: `UserMappingCliService.parseFromJson` flattened each account to `{email, awsAccountId}` and the backend's `CSVUserMappingParser` treated the column as an ignorable extra. The rule now implemented in one place — `WorkgroupAccountLinkService` — is that an account whose display name is `DevOps-x` belongs to the workgroup **`aws-DevOps-x`**: matched **exactly** on `"aws-" + display_name`, case-insensitively via `WorkgroupRepository.findByNameIgnoreCase`, and **created** (root level, `createdBy` = the acting ADMIN) when it does not exist. Suffixed variants such as `aws-DevOps-x-rolegreen` are deliberately not matched — a fuzzy rule here would hand an unrelated workgroup's members access to an account's assets, since a link is unified-asset-access **rule #9** (`WorkgroupAwsAccount`), not bookkeeping. docs/CHANGELOG.md:51:- **Full `excepted` recompute chunked to stop multi-minute lock holds (2026-08-24)** — `VulnerabilityRepository.recomputeExceptedAll()` was a single `UPDATE vulnerability v JOIN asset a … SET v.excepted = CASE WHEN EXISTS(…)` **with no WHERE clause**. It took exclusive row locks on every `vulnerability` row (~1.8M in production) and, through its correlated subquery, read locks on `vulnerability_exception` — holding both for the entire 53–180s transaction. Every concurrent writer to either table then blocked until lock-wait-timeout: bulk exception delete/import, CrowdStrike imports, per-asset recomputes. `DeadlockRetry` absorbed the failure, which is exactly why it stayed hidden — but the *other* operation still paid the full timeout first, observed as ~40s per `delete_all_vulnerability_exceptions` in both E2E runs, contending with "Async full excepted recompute complete: 1824736 rows in 53481 ms". Fix: `AsyncExceptionRecompute.recomputeAllChunked` drives the recompute as bounded **keyset** chunks (`CHUNK_SIZE` 10,000) through the new `recomputeExceptedForIdRange(afterId, throughId)`, each in its own REQUIRES_NEW transaction with per-chunk `DeadlockRetry`. Lock hold per transaction drops from minutes to milliseconds, so competing writers interleave between chunks instead of queueing behind one lock set; a chunk that loses a race replays only its own id range instead of the whole statement. **Keyset, not fixed-width id stepping** — the CrowdStrike import is delete-then-insert per asset, so ids are sparse and `MAX(id)` runs far ahead of the row count, which would make blind stepping spend most iterations on empty ranges. The daily 03:00 `recomputeAllExceptedScheduled` now delegates to the same driver (its orphaned `selfProvider` removed), so the nightly pass stops reintroducing the hold. Chunking gives up atomicity, and that is argued rather than assumed: the operation is already `@Async`, its documented contract is already eventual ("rows stay visible until it lands", failures "non-fatal; standing sweeps will retry"), a mid-statement failure already left partial state, and readers evaluate `v.excepted = 0` per row without a cross-table snapshot — so no guarantee is lost, and a failure now leaves a converged *prefix* rather than nothing. `recomputeExceptedAll()` is retained for the two integration tests that need single-step determinism on a tiny table, documented as not-for-production. Tests: `AsyncExceptionRecomputeChunkingTest` (5 cases pinning the traversal — sparse ids covered exactly once, half-open boundaries abutting without re-processing, no single range spanning the table) plus a `ExceptedFlagSqlAgreementIntegrationTest` case asserting the chunked statement assigns exactly what the atomic one does against a real database, with every flag pre-flipped so a skipped row cannot coincidentally match. Closes the `recomputeAll` lock-hold item open since the 2026-07-20 DB-pool work. OWASP: A01 reviewed — both new native queries bind parameters and take only primary-key boundaries from the preceding keyset read, on `@Async`/`@Scheduled` paths unreachable from any request.
docs/CHANGELOG.md:53:- **Vulnerability SLA anchored to remediation availability (2026-08-24)** — `secman.vulnerability.use-patch-publication-date` now defaults to **true** (both `application.yml` and the `VulnerabilitySettings` data class, which had to be changed together — they disagreed, and a new `VulnerabilitySettingsDefaultTest` now pins both). Age is measured from when a **fix became available**, falling back to CrowdStrike detection age per row when no patch date is published. Rationale: detection age answers "how long have we known", which resets whenever a host is rebuilt or newly onboarded — a 2023 CVE on a month-old host read as a month old — while remediation age answers "how long could we have fixed this and did not" and does not reward re-imaging. This only became possible in the same change that made the field arrive at all: the CLI batch payload had been dropping `patchPublicationDate` entirely, so the flag was inert on the production import path, and the ad-hoc lookup path never populated the field either (its DTO construction set neither publication date, so "persist it on save" persisted null forever — both now use the shared `FalconTimestamps` extractors). Two consequences documented rather than discovered later: (1) **overdue counts jump** on the first import after the change, since a patch date is normally much earlier than the detection date, so expect an outsized notification run; (2) **it is a one-way door** — `first_seen_at` is preserved as `min(prior, new)` across re-imports (the property that stops a re-import resetting the SLA clock), so once an import writes the older patch date, setting the flag back to false does **not** restore the previous anchors. A genuine revert is `UPDATE vulnerability SET first_seen_at = NULL WHERE source = 'CROWDSTRIKE'` plus a full re-import with the flag off. `requirePatchPublicationDate` stays **false** and is pinned by test: despite the near-identical name it is a *filter*, not an anchor, and enabling it would drop every vulnerability with no published patch date — hiding risk rather than re-dating it. Nothing changes until the next import; existing rows keep their current anchors. `docs/CROWDSTRIKE_IMPORT.md` §Timestamp fix, `docs/ENVIRONMENT.md`.
docs/CHANGELOG.md:55:- **CrowdStrike date semantics: three dates untangled (2026-08-24)** — reported as "the import is wrong: a 2023 CVE cannot be only 226 days old". Investigation showed the arithmetic was right and the *meaning* was not, plus four real defects underneath. Falcon's `created_timestamp` is when Spotlight created that finding **on that host**, and it creates every finding against a package in one batch — so a host legitimately shows one identical age across dozens of CVEs. Confirmed on live data: `detectedAt` clusters (80 rows on one date, 60 on another) while the newly captured `cve.published_date` spreads across dozens. Also confirmed that a CVE's ID year is its *reservation* year — `CVE-2023-53178` in this estate has `published_date = 2025-09-15` — so "a 2023 CVE can't be 62 days old" was never a sound inference; the data to see that simply was not being captured. Fixes: (1) **`extractPatchPublicationDate` asked `cve.published_date` FIRST**, so the column named for a patch — and used as the SLA anchor when `VULN_USE_PATCH_PUBLICATION_DATE=true` — usually held the CVE *disclosure* date, silently answering "how long since a fix existed?" with "how long since the CVE was published". Genuine remediation dates (`remediation.vendor_release_date`, `remediation.published_date`) now win; the CVE fields are kept as the **last** resort rather than removed, because `require-patch-publication-date` filters imports on this being non-null and narrowing it would have silently dropped rows — nothing that was non-null before becomes null. (2) **Timezone bug**: `CrowdStrikeVulnerabilityService.parseDetectionTimestamp` (the ad-hoc lookup behind the reported screen) parsed `"2026-01-10T22:18:26Z"` by *stripping* the `Z` and handing the rest to `LocalDateTime.parse`, relabelling a UTC instant as system-local instead of converting it — a whole-day shift across midnight, since age is `ChronoUnit.DAYS.between`. There were **four** copies of Falcon date parsing, one correct; all now delegate to one new `FalconTimestamps`, which also returns **null rather than `now()`** for an absent/unreadable date (defaulting to now reads as "detected today" = zero days = never overdue, a security miss dressed as a formatting fallback). (3) **The high-volume CLI batch payload dropped every date**: `/api/crowdstrike/servers/import` hand-built a map of `cveId`/`severity`/`affectedProduct`/`daysOpen` only, so `patchPublicationDate` was always null on the main import path and `VULN_USE_PATCH_PUBLICATION_DATE` could never take effect there at all. It now also sends `detectedAt` and both publication dates, and the backend prefers `detectedAt` over re-deriving `importTimestamp − daysOpen` — the same cross-clock, twice-truncated reconstruction shape as the 2026-08-21 reconcile incident (`daysOpen` is still sent, and the reconstruction retained, so an older CLI keeps working). (4) Saving from the ad-hoc lookup dropped `patch_publication_date` entirely. New `cve_published_date` column (V259, nullable, not backfilled — the import is delete-then-insert, so rows acquire it on the next run) surfaced on the lookup page as a **CVE Published** column, with "Days Open" renamed to **Detected (days)** and tooltipped as "not the age of the CVE". Tests: `CrowdStrikeTimestampParsingTest` (8 cases pinning the timezone contract and unknown-stays-null), `FalconDateExtractionTest` (6 cases pinning the preference order *and* the deliberate CVE fallback). Three unrelated pre-existing failures that had been red on `main` were also fixed to get a green build: `ResponseControllerAccessControlTest` (four `Cannot infer type for type parameter 'O'` — backend test sources did not compile at all), `InstalledProductListServiceTest` ×2 (mockk had no stub for a `countProductsByServer` call the service gained), and `VulnerabilityServicePreviewIntegrationTest` (reflection lookup missing the `includeInstallerFindings` parameter added by product classification). `docs/CROWDSTRIKE_IMPORT.md` §Timestamp fix.
docs/CHANGELOG.md:57:- **EOL mails carry the affected-systems table (2026-08-24)** — both EOL mail paths now embed the same table the product drilldown page shows, rendered by one new `EolFindingTableRenderer`: System, Type, Cloud account, **Cloud instance**, AD domain, Version, Release cycle, End of support, Status (plus Component for the owner notification, which spans many products; the broadcast is one product, so that column would be a constant). Previously the "Contact affected owners" broadcast (`/vulnerabilities/eol/products/{product}`) sent only the admin's free-text message with **no findings data at all**, and `secman send-eol-notifications` sent a 4-column Component/Version/Cycle/EOL table with no account, instance, domain, type or status — a recipient mapped to a whole AWS account could not tell which system or which account a row belonged to. Pieces: (1) **`cloudInstanceId` denormalized onto `eol_finding`** (V258, nullable, populated by `EolScanService` at both `ASSET_*` insertion sites exactly as `assetName`/`cloudAccountId`/`assetOwner` already are) and surfaced on `EolFindingResponse`, the page table and the CSV export so page, CSV and mail agree; deliberately **not backfilled** — the scan is delete-then-insert, so existing rows acquire it on the next `eol-sync` and read `-` until then; (2) **per-recipient scoping of the broadcast** — `EolBroadcastRecipientResolver.resolve` now returns `EolBroadcastRecipient(user, assetIds)` instead of `List<User>`, carrying the asset ids that made each user a recipient, and `EmailBroadcastService` renders only those rows into that recipient's copy. That linkage (owner, manual creator, scan uploader, AWS-account mapping, AD-domain mapping) is criteria 3/4/5/6/8 of §Unified Asset Access, hence provably a subset of what the recipient may already see (§A01) at **zero extra access queries** and with no way to drift from the rule that produced the recipient; sending one shared table would have disclosed other tenants' hostnames and account ids to every owner on the list. Manually-entered Cc addresses ride along on the owner's message and see that owner's rows only; (3) **bounded output** — rows and count are both taken at the query (`findByComponentNameForAssets` page of 200 + `countByComponentNameForAssets`), never fetched whole and sliced in Kotlin (§A04), and the remainder is disclosed in the table footer rather than silently truncated; (4) **one escaping sink** — the renderer escapes at assembly and strips CR/LF from the text part, replacing `EolNotificationService`'s private `escapeHtml`/`sanitizeForText` (which also escaped *before* truncating, so a 512-char cut could split an entity); the table is generated server-side at send time and never passes `EmailBroadcastService.sanitizeBroadcastHtml`, whose safelist strips every attribute except `a[href|title]` and would have removed the inline styles mail clients need. The compose modal now says the table is appended automatically and is scoped per recipient. Unrelated pre-existing breakage fixed to reach a green build: `ResponseControllerAccessControlTest` failed to compile on `main` (four `Cannot infer type for type parameter 'O'` on single-arg `exchange(...)`), so backend test sources did not build at all. `docs/EOL.md` §5.1.

docs/CHANGELOG.md:51:- **Full `excepted` recompute chunked to stop multi-minute lock holds (2026-08-24)** — `VulnerabilityRepository.recomputeExceptedAll()` was a single `UPDATE vulnerability v JOIN asset a … SET v.excepted = CASE WHEN EXISTS(…)` **with no WHERE clause**. It took exclusive row locks on every `vulnerability` row (~1.8M in production) and, through its correlated subquery, read locks on `vulnerability_exception` — holding both for the entire 53–180s transaction. Every concurrent writer to either table then blocked until lock-wait-timeout: bulk exception delete/import, CrowdStrike imports, per-asset recomputes. `DeadlockRetry` absorbed the failure, which is exactly why it stayed hidden — but the *other* operation still paid the full timeout first, observed as ~40s per `delete_all_vulnerability_exceptions` in both E2E runs, contending with "Async full excepted recompute complete: 1824736 rows in 53481 ms". Fix: `AsyncExceptionRecompute.recomputeAllChunked` drives the recompute as bounded **keyset** chunks (`CHUNK_SIZE` 10,000) through the new `recomputeExceptedForIdRange(afterId, throughId)`, each in its own REQUIRES_NEW transaction with per-chunk `DeadlockRetry`. Lock hold per transaction drops from minutes to milliseconds, so competing writers interleave between chunks instead of queueing behind one lock set; a chunk that loses a race replays only its own id range instead of the whole statement. **Keyset, not fixed-width id stepping** — the CrowdStrike import is delete-then-insert per asset, so ids are sparse and `MAX(id)` runs far ahead of the row count, which would make blind stepping spend most iterations on empty ranges. The daily 03:00 `recomputeAllExceptedScheduled` now delegates to the same driver (its orphaned `selfProvider` removed), so the nightly pass stops reintroducing the hold. Chunking gives up atomicity, and that is argued rather than assumed: the operation is already `@Async`, its documented contract is already eventual ("rows stay visible until it lands", failures "non-fatal; standing sweeps will retry"), a mid-statement failure already left partial state, and readers evaluate `v.excepted = 0` per row without a cross-table snapshot — so no guarantee is lost, and a failure now leaves a converged *prefix* rather than nothing. `recomputeExceptedAll()` is retained for the two integration tests that need single-step determinism on a tiny table, documented as not-for-production. Tests: `AsyncExceptionRecomputeChunkingTest` (5 cases pinning the traversal — sparse ids covered exactly once, half-open boundaries abutting without re-processing, no single range spanning the table) plus a `ExceptedFlagSqlAgreementIntegrationTest` case asserting the chunked statement assigns exactly what the atomic one does against a real database, with every flag pre-flipped so a skipped row cannot coincidentally match. Closes the `recomputeAll` lock-hold item open since the 2026-07-20 DB-pool work. OWASP: A01 reviewed — both new native queries bind parameters and take only primary-key boundaries from the preceding keyset read, on `@Async`/`@Scheduled` paths unreachable from any request.
docs/CHANGELOG.md:53:- **Vulnerability SLA anchored to remediation availability (2026-08-24)** — `secman.vulnerability.use-patch-publication-date` now defaults to **true** (both `application.yml` and the `VulnerabilitySettings` data class, which had to be changed together — they disagreed, and a new `VulnerabilitySettingsDefaultTest` now pins both). Age is measured from when a **fix became available**, falling back to CrowdStrike detection age per row when no patch date is published. Rationale: detection age answers "how long have we known", which resets whenever a host is rebuilt or newly onboarded — a 2023 CVE on a month-old host read as a month old — while remediation age answers "how long could we have fixed this and did not" and does not reward re-imaging. This only became possible in the same change that made the field arrive at all: the CLI batch payload had been dropping `patchPublicationDate` entirely, so the flag was inert on the production import path, and the ad-hoc lookup path never populated the field either (its DTO construction set neither publication date, so "persist it on save" persisted null forever — both now use the shared `FalconTimestamps` extractors). Two consequences documented rather than discovered later: (1) **overdue counts jump** on the first import after the change, since a patch date is normally much earlier than the detection date, so expect an outsized notification run; (2) **it is a one-way door** — `first_seen_at` is preserved as `min(prior, new)` across re-imports (the property that stops a re-import resetting the SLA clock), so once an import writes the older patch date, setting the flag back to false does **not** restore the previous anchors. A genuine revert is `UPDATE vulnerability SET first_seen_at = NULL WHERE source = 'CROWDSTRIKE'` plus a full re-import with the flag off. `requirePatchPublicationDate` stays **false** and is pinned by test: despite the near-identical name it is a *filter*, not an anchor, and enabling it would drop every vulnerability with no published patch date — hiding risk rather than re-dating it. Nothing changes until the next import; existing rows keep their current anchors. `docs/CROWDSTRIKE_IMPORT.md` §Timestamp fix, `docs/ENVIRONMENT.md`.
docs/CHANGELOG.md:55:- **CrowdStrike date semantics: three dates untangled (2026-08-24)** — reported as "the import is wrong: a 2023 CVE cannot be only 226 days old". Investigation showed the arithmetic was right and the *meaning* was not, plus four real defects underneath. Falcon's `created_timestamp` is when Spotlight created that finding **on that host**, and it creates every finding against a package in one batch — so a host legitimately shows one identical age across dozens of CVEs. Confirmed on live data: `detectedAt` clusters (80 rows on one date, 60 on another) while the newly captured `cve.published_date` spreads across dozens. Also confirmed that a CVE's ID year is its *reservation* year — `CVE-2023-53178` in this estate has `published_date = 2025-09-15` — so "a 2023 CVE can't be 62 days old" was never a sound inference; the data to see that simply was not being captured. Fixes: (1) **`extractPatchPublicationDate` asked `cve.published_date` FIRST**, so the column named for a patch — and used as the SLA anchor when `VULN_USE_PATCH_PUBLICATION_DATE=true` — usually held the CVE *disclosure* date, silently answering "how long since a fix existed?" with "how long since the CVE was published". Genuine remediation dates (`remediation.vendor_release_date`, `remediation.published_date`) now win; the CVE fields are kept as the **last** resort rather than removed, because `require-patch-publication-date` filters imports on this being non-null and narrowing it would have silently dropped rows — nothing that was non-null before becomes null. (2) **Timezone bug**: `CrowdStrikeVulnerabilityService.parseDetectionTimestamp` (the ad-hoc lookup behind the reported screen) parsed `"2026-01-10T22:18:26Z"` by *stripping* the `Z` and handing the rest to `LocalDateTime.parse`, relabelling a UTC instant as system-local instead of converting it — a whole-day shift across midnight, since age is `ChronoUnit.DAYS.between`. There were **four** copies of Falcon date parsing, one correct; all now delegate to one new `FalconTimestamps`, which also returns **null rather than `now()`** for an absent/unreadable date (defaulting to now reads as "detected today" = zero days = never overdue, a security miss dressed as a formatting fallback). (3) **The high-volume CLI batch payload dropped every date**: `/api/crowdstrike/servers/import` hand-built a map of `cveId`/`severity`/`affectedProduct`/`daysOpen` only, so `patchPublicationDate` was always null on the main import path and `VULN_USE_PATCH_PUBLICATION_DATE` could never take effect there at all. It now also sends `detectedAt` and both publication dates, and the backend prefers `detectedAt` over re-deriving `importTimestamp − daysOpen` — the same cross-clock, twice-truncated reconstruction shape as the 2026-08-21 reconcile incident (`daysOpen` is still sent, and the reconstruction retained, so an older CLI keeps working). (4) Saving from the ad-hoc lookup dropped `patch_publication_date` entirely. New `cve_published_date` column (V259, nullable, not backfilled — the import is delete-then-insert, so rows acquire it on the next run) surfaced on the lookup page as a **CVE Published** column, with "Days Open" renamed to **Detected (days)** and tooltipped as "not the age of the CVE". Tests: `CrowdStrikeTimestampParsingTest` (8 cases pinning the timezone contract and unknown-stays-null), `FalconDateExtractionTest` (6 cases pinning the preference order *and* the deliberate CVE fallback). Three unrelated pre-existing failures that had been red on `main` were also fixed to get a green build: `ResponseControllerAccessControlTest` (four `Cannot infer type for type parameter 'O'` — backend test sources did not compile at all), `InstalledProductListServiceTest` ×2 (mockk had no stub for a `countProductsByServer` call the service gained), and `VulnerabilityServicePreviewIntegrationTest` (reflection lookup missing the `includeInstallerFindings` parameter added by product classification). `docs/CROWDSTRIKE_IMPORT.md` §Timestamp fix.
docs/CHANGELOG.md:57:- **EOL mails carry the affected-systems table (2026-08-24)** — both EOL mail paths now embed the same table the product drilldown page shows, rendered by one new `EolFindingTableRenderer`: System, Type, Cloud account, **Cloud instance**, AD domain, Version, Release cycle, End of support, Status (plus Component for the owner notification, which spans many products; the broadcast is one product, so that column would be a constant). Previously the "Contact affected owners" broadcast (`/vulnerabilities/eol/products/{product}`) sent only the admin's free-text message with **no findings data at all**, and `secman send-eol-notifications` sent a 4-column Component/Version/Cycle/EOL table with no account, instance, domain, type or status — a recipient mapped to a whole AWS account could not tell which system or which account a row belonged to. Pieces: (1) **`cloudInstanceId` denormalized onto `eol_finding`** (V258, nullable, populated by `EolScanService` at both `ASSET_*` insertion sites exactly as `assetName`/`cloudAccountId`/`assetOwner` already are) and surfaced on `EolFindingResponse`, the page table and the CSV export so page, CSV and mail agree; deliberately **not backfilled** — the scan is delete-then-insert, so existing rows acquire it on the next `eol-sync` and read `-` until then; (2) **per-recipient scoping of the broadcast** — `EolBroadcastRecipientResolver.resolve` now returns `EolBroadcastRecipient(user, assetIds)` instead of `List<User>`, carrying the asset ids that made each user a recipient, and `EmailBroadcastService` renders only those rows into that recipient's copy. That linkage (owner, manual creator, scan uploader, AWS-account mapping, AD-domain mapping) is criteria 3/4/5/6/8 of §Unified Asset Access, hence provably a subset of what the recipient may already see (§A01) at **zero extra access queries** and with no way to drift from the rule that produced the recipient; sending one shared table would have disclosed other tenants' hostnames and account ids to every owner on the list. Manually-entered Cc addresses ride along on the owner's message and see that owner's rows only; (3) **bounded output** — rows and count are both taken at the query (`findByComponentNameForAssets` page of 200 + `countByComponentNameForAssets`), never fetched whole and sliced in Kotlin (§A04), and the remainder is disclosed in the table footer rather than silently truncated; (4) **one escaping sink** — the renderer escapes at assembly and strips CR/LF from the text part, replacing `EolNotificationService`'s private `escapeHtml`/`sanitizeForText` (which also escaped *before* truncating, so a 512-char cut could split an entity); the table is generated server-side at send time and never passes `EmailBroadcastService.sanitizeBroadcastHtml`, whose safelist strips every attribute except `a[href|title]` and would have removed the inline styles mail clients need. The compose modal now says the table is appended automatically and is scoped per recipient. Unrelated pre-existing breakage fixed to reach a green build: `ResponseControllerAccessControlTest` failed to compile on `main` (four `Cannot infer type for type parameter 'O'` on single-arg `exchange(...)`), so backend test sources did not build at all. `docs/EOL.md` §5.1.
